--- title: "Appendix 2C: Splines" --- - Sometimes polynomials do not model nonlinearities well enough - E.g., Too many turns in the line, very quick changes of direction, etc. - Splines allow you to specify a structural "break" (AKA a "knot") in the regression line - Slope can be completely different before and after the knot (e.g., before and after age 60) - Estimate separate coefficient for age \< 60 and age ≥ 60 - Parametric technique; you get a coefficient (and associated SE/CI/*p*-value) for the slope between each knot - Works with almost any regression model - I give only a quick introduction here. For details on splines, [Marsh and Cormier's 2002 Sage QASS](https://methods.sagepub.com/book/spline-regression-models) book is a good and accessible introduction to splines - Also see [Edwards and Parry 2018](https://doi.org/10.1177/1094428117715067) - See [Appendix A2.8](appendix-2a/a2-8-splines.qmd) and [**mkspline**](https://www.stata.com/manuals/rmkspline.pdf) for some details on cubic splines which combine splines and nonlinearities ![](images/spline-example.png){width=50% fig-alt="Scatterplot with a linear spline: a line that falls to a knot and then rises."} ## Linear splines - How do we estimate the two different slopes shown on the graph above? - Create two variables for *x*: one summarizes the relationship \< 60 and one for the relationship ≥ 60 - Note 60 is the "knot" placement - First variable summarizes relationship for age \< 60. Defined as: $${age}_{< 60} = original\ value\ of\ age\ if\ age < 60$$ $${age}_{< 60} = 60\ if\ age \geq 60$$ - Second variable summarizes relationship for $age \geq 60$. Defined as age difference from last knot: $${age}_{\geq 60} = 0\ if\ age \leq 60$$ $${age}_{\geq 60} = \#\ of\ years\ since\ last\ knot\ (age\ 60)$$ - For example, age 65 is coded as 5 on ${age}_{\geq 60}$; age 80 is coded as 20 on ${age}_{\geq 60}$ ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## Stata ```{.stata-run} . use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/cda_gss", clear (cda_gss.dta | GSS 1972-2021 CDA - Categorical Data Analysis | date created 202 > 3) . . lpoly samesexop year, /// > xlab(1974(4)2018) ylab(1(1)4) noscatter ci legend(off) /// > ytitle("Support for same-gender relationships") /// > subtitle("Local polynomial smoothing") /// > title("[2.7.a] Change in supportive attitudes toward same-gender relations > hips from 1972 to 2020") ``` ![](fig/cda-02_07_a-splines-01.png){width=80% fig-alt="Local polynomial smooth of support for same-gender relationships by survey year: flat until about 1990, then rising, with changes in slope around 1996 and 2006."} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(haven) # import Stata data and labels library(dplyr) # data manipulation library(ggplot2) # graphs library(modelsummary) # regression tables library(marginaleffects) # predictions and marginal effects library(lspline) # linear splines library(cleanplots) # graph scheme cleanplots_defaults() gss <- read_dta("https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/cda_gss.dta") # Keep only the variables used and drop any missing data on them gss <- gss[c("samesexop", "year")] gss <- gss[complete.cases(gss), ] gss <- gss |> mutate(samesexop = as.numeric(samesexop)) ggplot(gss, aes(x = year, y = samesexop)) + geom_smooth() + scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1974, 2018, 4)) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:4, limits = c(1, 4)) + labs(title = "[2.7.a] Change in supportive attitudes toward same-gender relationships", subtitle = "Local polynomial smoothing", x = "Year of survey", y = "Support for same-gender relationships") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](appendix-2c-splines_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-1-1.png){fig-alt='Local polynomial smooth of support for same-gender relationships by survey year: flat until about 1990, then rising, with changes in slope around 1996 and 2006.' width=80%} ::: ::: ::: \*Where would you place the "knots" to model this with splines? ### Interpreting linear splines - Linear splines specify linear relationships between each "knot" - I chose knots at 1990, 1996, and 2006 based on graph above - Here are the variables we need: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## Stata ```{.stata-run} . mkspline year_lt90 1990 year_90_96 1996 year_96_06 2006 year_06_18 = year . codebook year*, c Variable Obs Unique Mean Min Max Label -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- year 68846 33 1996.465 1972 2021 gss year for this respondent year1972 68846 33 24.46544 0 49 Years since 1972 year_lt90 68846 17 1986.615 1972 1990 year: (.,1990) year_90_96 68846 5 3.443904 0 6 year: (1990,1996) year_96_06 68846 6 4.058014 0 10 year: (1996,2006) year_06_18 68846 8 2.348662 0 15 year: (2006,.) -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ``` ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # lspline() makes one variable for each piece of the spline summary(lspline(gss$year, knots = c(1990, 1996, 2006))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` r-output 1 2 3 4 Min. :1973 Min. :0.000 Min. : 0.000 Min. : 0.000 1st Qu.:1984 1st Qu.:0.000 1st Qu.: 0.000 1st Qu.: 0.000 Median :1990 Median :6.000 Median : 0.000 Median : 0.000 Mean :1987 Mean :3.293 Mean : 3.838 Mean : 2.564 3rd Qu.:1990 3rd Qu.:6.000 3rd Qu.:10.000 3rd Qu.: 2.000 Max. :1990 Max. :6.000 Max. :10.000 Max. :15.000 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## Stata ```{.stata-run} . reg samesexop year_lt90 year_90_96 year_96_06 year_06_18 Source | SS df MS Number of obs = 40,270 -------------+---------------------------------- F(4, 40265) = 1442.27 Model | 9128.86223 4 2282.21556 Prob > F = 0.0000 Residual | 63714.2247 40,265 1.5823724 R-squared = 0.1253 -------------+---------------------------------- Adj R-squared = 0.1252 Total | 72843.0869 40,269 1.80891224 Root MSE = 1.2579 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ samesexop | Coefficient Std. err. t P>|t| [95% conf. interval] -------------+---------------------------------------------------------------- year_lt90 | -0.004 0.002 -2.562 0.010 -0.008 -0.001 year_90_96 | 0.078 0.004 17.418 0.000 0.069 0.087 year_96_06 | 0.016 0.003 5.502 0.000 0.010 0.021 year_06_18 | 0.056 0.002 28.645 0.000 0.053 0.060 _cons | 10.155 3.340 3.040 0.002 3.609 16.702 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ . est store splinemod . est table splinemod, /// > title("[2.7.b] Spline regression model for opinion of same-gender relation > ships") /// > b(%5.3f) star(.05 .01 .001) [2.7.b] Spline regression model for opinion of same-gender relationships --------------------------- Variable | splinemod -------------+------------- year_lt90 | -0.004* year_90_96 | 0.078*** year_96_06 | 0.016*** year_06_18 | 0.056*** _cons | 10.155** --------------------------- Legend: * p<.05; ** p<.01; *** p<.001 ``` ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} splinemod <- lm(samesexop ~ lspline(year, knots = c(1990, 1996, 2006)), data = gss) modelsummary(splinemod, stars = c("*" = .05, "**" = .01, "***" = .001), title = "[2.7.b] Spline regression model for opinion of same-gender relationships") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
